State of Chhattisgarh through the Incharge Police Station Balodabazar District :
Balodabazar-Bhathapara, Chhattisgarh ...

Appellant
 versus
Mukesh Yadav S/o Vedprakash Yadav Aged About 20 Years R/o Village Semhardih,
Post Nipaniya, Police Station Bhatapra ( Rural ) District : Balodabazar-Bhathapara,
Chhattisgarh ...

Respondent
For Appellant/State : Mr. Ranbir Singh Marhas, Addl.

Advocate General For Respondent :
Ms.Smriti Ekka, Advocate on behalf of Legal Aid (Goutam Bhaduri, Judge) C A V Judgment
1.

The present appeal is against the judgment dated 07.11.2017 passed by the learned Special Judge
(Ftc), Balodabazar (Cg) in Criminal Case (Pocso Act) No.35/2017 (State Vs. Mukesh Yadav)
whereby the respondent has been acquitted of the charges under section 363, 366, 376 of Ipc read
with section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act by giving benefit of doubt.
2.

The case of the prosecution is that complainant (U) lodged a written complaint at Police Chowki Karhibazar stating that on 07.04.2017 at 12.30 p.m., when he woke up at 12.30 a.m., in the night to pick Mahua seeds he saw that the victim was not sleeping with her aunt (Mami) and thereafter he searched for victim and when he did not find her, he made a phone call to father of victim Puranlal Verma and informed him that his daughter was not in the house.
A report was made Digitally A signed by ANNAJEE A RAO ANNAJEE RAO against the unknown person.
Subsequently on 09.04.2017, the victim was recovered from the house of father of respondent (V) and seizure memo Ex.P-2 was prepared.
Thereafter the statement of victim was recorded and she was subjected to medical examination.
Having been found that the prosecutrix was minor and she was enticed away by the accused from the lawful custody of the guardian, charge sheet was filed against him.
3. The respondent abjured the guilt and claimed to be tried.
The prosecution examined as many as 10 witnesses and exhibited 24 documents.

The learned Special Judge, after evaluating evidence came to a finding that no offence would be made out and the prosecution has failed to prove the State Of Chhattisgarh vs Mukesh Yadav on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99686486/
1 offence beyond reasonable doubt, thereby the trial has ended with acquittal.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/State would submit that the date of birth of the victim was shown to be 03.05.1999 in Dakhil Kharij register (Ex.P-19C) which is proved by Head Master (P.W.5) and this fact is further supported by Kotwari Register seized vide Ex.P-10, consequently on the date of incident, the victim was minor as she was aged below 18 years.
He would further submit that reading of statements of other witnesses which are on record would show that the offence was made out and the learned Sessions Judge was wrong in dismissing the appeal.

5(i). Per contra,
learned Counsel for the respondent would submit that the victim herself has not supported the case of prosecution.

She refers to the statement of victim under section 164 CrPC and submits that the victim herself has categorically deposed that respondent has not committed any officence and no incident took place with her.

5(ii) She would submit that so far as the age of prosecutrix is concerned, she herself stated in cross examination that her DoB is 03.05.1998 and Annexure P-2 Seizure Panchnama also stated that she is more than 17 years on the date of incident.
Therefore, the prosecution itself was not sure about the minority of victim.

5(iii) She would further submit that the entry made in Kotwar register (Ex.P-10)
has been exhibited before the trial Court but the Kotwar (SD) who made the entry of in the Register has not been examined before the trial Court to prove the age of victim, therefore, the Kotwari Register has not been proved as per Section 35 of the Evidence Act.

5(iv) She would further submit that according to the statement of prosecutrix, no offence was committed with her which further stands corroborated by FSL (Ex.P- 23) and the Doctor has also found no injury over the body of victim.
Therefore, if the categorical statement of victim coupled with medical report as also FSL report is considered, no offence can be attributed to the respondent.
Hence, the acquittal of respondent is well merited which do not call for any interference.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and have also perused the records.
The victim (Y) is examined as P.W.3.
She has stated that no incident took place with her and nothing has been committed by the respondent and even she does not identify the accused.
In examination-in-chief she has stated that her date of birth is 03.05.1998 and when a suggestion was given about her date of birth, she expressed her ignorance.
The mother is examined as P.W.3.
She has stated that since the victim went out without informing to any one, the report was made to Police and the offence was registered.
7. In order to prove the age, the Dakhil Kharij register Annexure P-19(C) was placed on record which is proved by P.W.5 the Head Master and as per the document, the DoB was recorded as 03.05.1999.
However, the statement of P.W.5, would show that he was not the author of document and it has not been stated that he was present while her initial admission was made in the school.
The seizure memo shows that village Kotwari register showing the details of births and death was seized from Kotwar S.D. vide Ex.P-10 wherein the DoB of victim was shown to be 03.05.1999.

The Kotwari register though has been exhibited before the trial Court but neither the Kotwar Santu Das who State Of Chhattisgarh vs Mukesh Yadav on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99686486/

sentences.text: 2 made the entry regarding DoB of victim in the register was examined nor the Kotwari register was produced to prove the age of prosecutrix as per section 35 of the Evidence Act.
Only the seizure memo has been produced.
It is well settled legal proposition that the entry in the Kotwar Register cannot be relied upon unless its probate value in terms of provisions of section 35 of the Evidence Act is proved.

8. The Supreme Court in Babloo Pasi v. State of Jharkhan (2008) 13 SCC 133 held that the School register is relevant and admissible but is not of much evidentiary value in absence of the material on which the age was recorded.

entities.text: Babloo Pasi v. State of Jharkhan (2008) 13 SCC 133
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Para 28 is relevant and quoted below:
"28.

It is trite that to render a document admissible under Section 35, three conditions have to be satisfied, namely : (i) entry that is relied on must be one in a public or other official book, register or record; (ii) it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or a relevant fact, and (iii) it must be made by a public servant in discharge of his official duties, or in performance of his duty especially enjoined by law.

An entry relating to date of birth made in the School register is relevant and admissible under Section 35 of the Act but the entry regarding the age of a person in a school register is of not much evidentiary value to prove the age of the person in the absence of the material on which the age was recorded.
(See Birad Mal Singhvi v. Anand Purohit 1988 Supp SCC 604."

entities.text: Birad Mal Singhvi v. Anand Purohit 1988 Supp SCC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above legal position to the facts of present case for determining the age of victim, we are of the considered view that the entry regarding the age of victim in a school register is of not much evidentiary value to prove the age of prosecutrix in absence of material on which the age was recorded.

Therefore, this benefit would lean in favour of the respondent and appreciation of the entire evidence would show that the prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was minor on the date of incident on 07.04.2017.
9.

So far as the allegation of offence u/s 363, 366 and 376 IPC is concerned, the mother P.W.2 has not supported the case of prosecution and the victim herself has completely denied the commission of any office.

Even in the statement u/s 164 CrPC which is marked as Ex.P-20, the victim has clearly admitted the fact that no offence was committed with her and further her statement stood firm by Dr. N.G. (P.W.4) who has deposed that there were no marks of struggle on the body of the victim.
She has further deposed that during examination she did not notice any pain on the body or genitals of victim.
The MLC report is Ex.P-17 wherein the doctor opined that there was no sign of struggle.

The vaginal slide was also prepared and when it was sent for FSL examination along with under-garments which is said to have been containing spermatozoa, the result was revealed by the FSL report dated 08.06.2017 wherein the semen stains and human sperm were not found in Articles A B C D.
10.
On an over-all analysis of evidence and facts situation of the case, we hold that no offence of rape is made out against the respondent.

Hence, we do not find any merit in the appeal warranting State Of Chhattisgarh vs Mukesh Yadav on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99686486/
3 interference in the judgment of acquittal.
